\begin{frame}{My Brain: three layers of one system}
\subt{\chg{Three top-level folders, each with one job: shared rules, one folder per project, and hidden tooling.}}
\begin{columns}[c,onlytextwidth]\column{.565\textwidth}
\begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{.48em}\small
\item \textbf{general/.} Shared indexes, global decisions, profiles, tool policies and agent protocols.
\item \textbf{areas/.} Research, Grant, Teaching and Other; a self-contained memory per project.
\item \textbf{.infra/.} Hidden scripts and tool runtimes; not canonical project knowledge.
\item \textbf{Source of truth.} Markdown in general/ and areas/; other backends are supporting layers.
\end{itemize}
\column{.405\textwidth}
\sboxblue{Real vault}{Brain/Marco on Dropbox; Desktop alias points to the same folder.}
\sboxblue{Core principle}{Global routing first; load one project’s memory, not every project.}
\end{columns}
\tagline{One durable structure, multiple agents and many research activities.}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{One Brain, many Economics projects}
\subt{Each project has its own context and methodological decisions.}
\begin{columns}[c,onlytextwidth]\column{.565\textwidth}
\begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{.48em}\small
\item \textbf{Mafia Culture.} Artist, work, recording and video distinctions; verified sourcing and genre classification.
\item \textbf{Fragmented Opposition.} Repeatable news-collection workflow with failed-only retries and deterministic merges.
\item \textbf{Mafia Incendi.} Research code and Stata folders; unresolved questions remain visibly flagged.
\item \textbf{Other areas.} \chg{Grants, teaching and governance of the Brain itself.}
\end{itemize}
\column{.405\textwidth}
\sboxblue{Cross-project memory}{A skill moves to the global catalog only when it is reusable for different projects.}
\end{columns}
\medskip
\tagline{The Brain preserves why decisions were made, not only the latest output.}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Anatomy of a research project}
\subt{Different kinds of information have distinct filenames and lifecycles.}
\begin{columns}[c,onlytextwidth]\column{.565\textwidth}
\begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{.48em}\small
\item \textbf{INDEX / PROJECT\_BRIEF.} Navigation and stable problem definition.
\item \textbf{CURRENT\_STATE / NEXT\_ACTIONS.} Current progress and actionable restart point.
\item \textbf{DECISIONS / AGENT\_MEMORY.} Approved choices and durable constraints for future agents.
\item \textbf{SOURCES / TECHNICAL\_NOTES / LOG.} Provenance, commands and historical trace; optional wiki and session summaries.
\end{itemize}
\column{.405\textwidth}
\sboxblue{\chg{Why one file per question?}}{\chg{Each file answers one question: where are we, what did we decide, what comes next. To pick up the analysis, the agent opens CURRENT\_STATE and NEXT\_ACTIONS and skips the rest.}}
\sboxblue{Human benefit}{A new coauthor can see what is known, blocked and contested.}
\end{columns}
\tagline{Project memory = state + evidence + decisions + procedures.}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{The tool stack around the Brain}
\subt{The vault is the center; individual tools add functions.}
\begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{0.85em}
\item \textbf{Authoring / sync.} Obsidian, Markdown, Dropbox and Git.
\item \textbf{Recall / access.} Memanto \chg{(a local memory the agent can search)}.
\item \textbf{Code context / compression.} \chg{CodeGraph (a map of the code base, so the agent finds functions without reading every file) and Headroom (compresses long tool outputs).}
\item \textbf{Procedures.} Caveman, Econoclast, anti-slop-prose and Overleaf workflow.
\end{itemize}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Skills live in the Brain, not one AI}
\begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{0.85em}
\item \textbf{Global procedures.} general/capabilities/skills/ holds reusable cross-project workflows.
\item \textbf{Local procedures.} areas/.../skills/ keeps assumptions close to a specific project.
\item \textbf{Native exposure.} .agents/skills/ makes selected skills available to compatible agents.
\item \textbf{Promotion rule.} Only tested recurring routines become global skills.
\end{itemize}
\medskip
\tagline{Catalog cheaply; load instructions only when a task needs them.}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{My LLM Wiki: core files first}
\subt{Karpathy’s cumulative wiki adapted to project-oriented scientific work.}
\begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{0.85em}
\item \textbf{Preserve.} Original conversations and source traces under the relevant project’s raw/ directory.
\item \textbf{Distill.} Update CURRENT\_STATE, DECISIONS, AGENT\_MEMORY and TECHNICAL\_NOTES first.
\item \textbf{Extend.} Use wiki/ for stable long-form pipelines, methods and architectures.
\item \textbf{Index.} Every wiki page must appear under the project INDEX’s Wiki section.
\end{itemize}
\tagline{\chg{Update the short core files first. Write a long wiki page only for material that will not change often, such as a data pipeline.}}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Bootstrap → work → closeout → restart}
\subt{A reproducible routine makes independent sessions part of one project.}
\begin{columns}[c,onlytextwidth]
\column{.47\textwidth}\begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{.5em}\small
\item \textbf{Bootstrap.} Global INDEX and memory router → specific project files → skills only if relevant.
\item \textbf{Work.} Run tools and check evidence, errors, current code and open assumptions.
\item \textbf{Closeout.} Update state, next actions, decisions, technical notes and concise session log.
\item \textbf{Restart.} A new agent recovers a compact, trustworthy entry point rather than old chat context.
\end{itemize}
\column{.5\textwidth}
\begin{chgfig}

\tagline{\chg{The next session should open the state file and start working, not dig through old chats to find out what happened.}}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{A Brain also accumulates maintenance debt}
\subt{More files are not necessarily more useful knowledge.}
\begin{columns}[c,onlytextwidth]\column{.485\textwidth}
\sboxblue{Stale state}{Completed tasks still shown as next actions; paths point to old locations.}
\column{.485\textwidth}
\coursebox{Broken navigation}{Orphan wiki pages, missing references and outdated indexes.}
\end{columns}\vspace{1mm}
\begin{columns}[c,onlytextwidth]\column{.485\textwidth}
\sboxblue{Contradictions}{Competing claims or decisions, with no explicit resolution history.}
\column{.485\textwidth}
\coursebox{Duplicate procedures}{Slightly divergent skills and templates across projects or agents.}
\end{columns}\vspace{1mm}
\tagline{Maintenance is part of the memory architecture.}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{My Sunday Brain maintenance: a real audit}
{\small\bfseries What the Sunday agent checks, in order}\par\vspace{0.35em}
\begin{enumerate}\setlength{\itemsep}{0.18em}\small
\item Read BOOTSTRAP and the vault index.
\item Commit and push a Git snapshot; scan file names for secrets.
\item Scan every note; ingest the week's raw chats into the core files.
\item Align each project's state; move finished actions to the LOG.
\item Update the projects dashboard and the dates in MEMORY.md.
\item Fix dead links and paths that point to old locations.
\item Check that every wiki page is listed in its project INDEX.
\item Delete duplicates and backups, recoverable from the snapshot.
\item Look for sensitive data (keys, IBAN, booking codes).
\item Check that Memanto runs locally; run validate\_vault.py.
\item \chg{Look for new plugins and tools worth adding.}
\item \chg{Update the plugins and tools already installed.}
\item Write the LOG and a closeout; ask me open questions.
\end{enumerate}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Keep humans in control of the Brain}
\subt{\chg{The agent does the maintenance; I review what it changed before the change becomes permanent.}}
\begin{columns}[c,onlytextwidth]\column{.565\textwidth}
\begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{.48em}\small
\item \textbf{Every session.} Distill durable findings; mark uncertainty and next action.
\item \textbf{Every review.} Check stale state, index completeness, contradictory memory and orphan files.
\item \textbf{Before changes.} Snapshot with Git, inspect diffs, exclude secrets and preserve evidence.
\item \textbf{After changes.} Validate and record what actually changed; test new-agent restart.
\end{itemize}
\column{.405\textwidth}
\sboxblue{Research payoff}{Lower re-entry cost, portable expertise, potentially stronger reproducibility.}
\sboxblue{Open question}{Does persistent curated memory outperform pure chat and RAG on longitudinal research tasks? Test it.}
\end{columns}
\medskip
\tagline{JARVIS depends not only on a model, but on reliable memory, tools and governance.}
\end{frame}
